promise: Cut regulated child-care fees to an average of $10 per day across Canada by 2026.
description: Budget 2021 announced C$30B over five years to bring average regulated child-care fees to $10/day by 2025-26, via agreements with provinces. Fees were roughly halved in most provinces, but by 2025 only about 150,000 of 250,000 promised spaces existed, Alberta and Saskatchewan refused to sign the renewal, and the $10 average was not reached in several provinces.
evidence: Budget 2021 commitment of C$30B over five years
Only ~150,000 of 250,000 promised spaces created by March 2025
Alberta and Saskatchewan did not sign the March 2025 extension deal

promise: We will launch more than 10 live service games by fiscal 2025 (as reported).
description: Sony's 2021 strategy meeting set a target of more than 10 PlayStation live-service titles by end of fiscal 2025. Only a handful shipped (Helldivers 2, MLB The Show, Concord), Concord was shut down within weeks, and several announced live-service projects (including Naughty Dog's The Last of Us Factions) were cancelled in 2023-2024.
evidence: Sony IR presentation projected 10+ live service games by FY2025
The Last of Us Factions cancelled Dec 2023; multiple live service projects dropped 2024; Concord failed
Helldivers 2 (2024) succeeded as a live service title

promise: Reduce growth in day-to-day federal government spending from about 9% per year to under 2%
description: In the May 2025 throne speech, Carney promised measures to cut annual growth in the federal operating budget from about 9% under the previous government to below 2%. By September 2025 commentators reported the target had already been abandoned in the fall budget outlook, which projected spending growth well above 2%.
evidence: September 2025 reports said the fall budget outlook abandoned the under-2% target

promise: A GPT-6-level model will be released in Q1 2026
description: In a December 2025 interview Altman said OpenAI's next GPT-6-level model upgrade was expected in the first quarter of 2026, and he repeated that timing in a January 2026 roadmap discussion. Q1 passed without a release; OpenAI shipped GPT-5.5 on April 23, 2026 instead. As of early August 2026 GPT-6 (reportedly codenamed 'Astra') had not been released, and reports said it could be named GPT-5.7.
evidence: No GPT-6 release in Q1 2026; GPT-5.5 shipped April 23, 2026
July-August 2026 reports: GPT-6/Astra not yet public, naming unresolved (GPT-6 vs GPT-5.7)

promise: AI will be writing 90% of code within 3-6 months, and essentially all code within 12 months
description: At a Council on Foreign Relations forum (March 2025), Amodei said AI would be writing 90% of the code software developers were in charge of within three to six months, and 'essentially all of the code' within twelve months. The 90% milestone was not reached by September 2025; independent researchers estimated in 2026 that it would take 9-15 months beyond the prediction even inside Anthropic, let alone industry-wide.
evidence: 90% milestone not met by the September 2025 target
2026 assessments: goal still 9-15 months away by reasonable operational definitions
